turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): righto, shoes off for a sec. weight and blood pressure before the doctor.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah. that waiting room, i can't hear myself think with the telly and the kids.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): blood pressure's one twenty over eighty. uh the cuff slipped. it's one thirty two over seventy eight. pulse 74, weight 79 kilos.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): g'day, dr patel. sorry about the wait. you've brought someone.
[SEG0005] person_4 (CAREGIVER): jess. support worker. i come so things actually get followed up.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): she acts like i'd do a runner. i'm fine, this is a waste of an arvo.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): what do you want sorted, then?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): nothing, really. spots on my face, and my periods are weird. mum kicked off so jess dragged me. spots and weird periods.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): weird in what way?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): they disappear for ages, then just show up. i've overdone it with night shifts at the cafe. end of story.
[SEG0011] person_4 (CAREGIVER): there's weight gain as well, and dark hairs on her chin. she shaves before work.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): it's peach fuzz, relax. i have gotten heavier. i feel like a wet rag after a shift. so what.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): how long have the spots and the irregular periods been going?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): umm, six months. no, that's not right. year twelve was two years ago and it had started already. so two years.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): and the weight and the chin hair?
[SEG0016] person_4 (CAREGIVER): the hair's been a good few months. weight since last summer, less than a year.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): if you say so. i'm not keeping score.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): let me see. inflamed spots along the jaw, coarse dark hairs on the chin. not loads, but they're there.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): any pain low in the tummy, or pain when you bleed?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): nah. no pain.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): could you be pregnant?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): no way. i'm not seeing anyone.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): bowels been okay?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): yeah, fine.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): what about your breathing, or chest pain?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): no. chest is fine, breathing's fine.

[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): thinking out loud, acne plus irregular cycles plus chin hair and the weight, that can be polycystic ovary syndrome. here's the plan. i'll start you on levlen, one combined pill a day, to settle the skin and the cycle, and we'll send you for bloods.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): i don't want tablets. my feet feel dead after a double shift. that's just standing all day, not something a pill fixes.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): fair. before i prescribe anything, any headaches, zigzags, sparkly vision?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): err, sometimes a headache and the edges go sparkly. i lie down, it passes. it's nothing.

[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): sparkly edges like that are an aura, so i'm changing the plan. no levlen, i don't start a combined pill with migraine aura. we'll do the tests and decide later, and nothing is started today.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): family wise, diabetes? i'd add glucose if there is.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): mum's got type two diabetes, years of it. not me though.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): okay. these are booked, not a wait and see. fasting glucose, hba1c, testosterone, lh and fsh, and a pelvic ultrasound to look at the ovaries.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): a scan. for pimples. sure.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): medicines in the last while, and any allergies?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): no allergies. i tried doxycyclin, fifty milligrams, no, a hundred milligrams once a day for two weeks, then i stopped. useless. nothing since.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): we'll leave that doxycycline off. do you smoke at all?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): never have. two or three beers on a saturday, max.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): jot down when you bleed. a brand new worst ever headache means emergency, not the clinic. otherwise i want you back in three weeks for these results, that's booked in.
[SEG0041] person_4 (CAREGIVER): i'll make sure she comes. she lives with her mum, i'll text her.
[SEG0042] person_1 (NURSE): i'll lock in the bloods, the pelvic scan and the three week review out the front.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): ta. frog in my throat, your aircon's dry as. just need water, not a diagnosis.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): water's by the desk. see you in three weeks.

spec.situation: Young woman with acne and irregular periods for two years, some facial hair, weight gain; mother had diabetes; bloods and pelvic scan planned; contraceptive pill discussed, not started.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

bad.reason: Tests planned, but fasting glucose/HbA1c linked to family diabetes risk, not explicitly PCOS indication.
bad.text: Fasting glucose, HbA1c, testosterone, LH and FSH (type=laboratory, status=planned, requested_by=doctor, indication=Possible polycystic ovary syndrome)

omissions.text: Negative finding asked and answered: no pain when bleeding/dysmenorrhoea.
Negative finding asked and answered: bowel habit okay/fine.
Negative finding asked and answered: no shortness of breath/breathing fine.
Negative finding asked and answered: no chest pain.
Planned medicine was changed: doctor initially proposed Levlen one combined pill daily for skin/cycle, but after history of visual aura decided not to prescribe it; nothing was started today.
Headache red flag advice was specifically 'a brand new worst ever headache' should go to emergency, not clinic.
Follow-up was not only desired but already booked/booked in for three weeks, with bloods and pelvic scan also to be locked in/booked.
